Manufactured by [[Sienar Fleet Systems/Legends|Sienar Fleet Systems]],<ref name="DB" /> '''Obsidian 8''' was a modified [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE/ln starfighter]] serving the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire's]] [[Obsidian Squadron/Legends|Obsidian Squadron]]<ref name="CCG" /> by the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]].<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Obsidian 8 was operated by [[OS-72-8]], a [[TIE pilot]] who was previously stationed aboard<ref name="CCG" /> the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer/Legends|Star Destroyer]]<ref name="CSWE">{{CSWECite|II|402|Obsidian Squadron}}</ref> [[Devastator/Legends|''Devastator'']]. Obsidian 8 was used most often to pursue raiders attempting to take refuge in the upper [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of nearby [[Planet/Legends|planets]].<ref name="CCG" />

In 3 [[Galactic Standard Calendar|ABY]], the Empire [[Occupation of Bespin|occupied]] the planet [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] with the goal of capturing the [[YT-1300 light freighter/Legends|YT-1300 light freighter]] [[Millennium Falcon/Legends|''Millennium Falcon'']]. When the ''Falcon'' escaped from Bespin's [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]],<ref name="NEC" /> Obsidian 8 was among the [[TIE series/Legends|TIE]] [[Starfighter/Legends|fighters]] that pursued the [[Freighter/Legends|freighter]] into [[Realspace/Legends|space]].<ref name="BtM">''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]''</ref> However, Obsidian Squadron was unsuccessful in their pursuit, and the ''Millennium Falcon'' evaded Imperial capture. Obsidian 8 was armed with a pair of [[L-s1 laser cannon/Legends|L-s1 laser cannons]].<ref name="ESB" />

==Behind the scenes==
Obsidian 8 first appeared in<ref name="ESB novel">[[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|''Star Wars Episode V: The Empire Strikes Back'' novelization]]</ref> the [[April 12]], [[1980]]<ref name="Year by Year">''[[Star Wars Year By Year: A Visual History, Updated and Expanded Edition]]''</ref><ref name="Amazon-RandomHouse">{{Amazon|url=Empire-Strikes-Back-Storybook/dp/0394844149|text=The Empire Strikes Back Storybook}} {{C|US hardcover}}</ref> [[Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back (novelization)|novelization]] of the ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[original trilogy]] film {{Film|V}},<ref name="ESB novel" /> simultaneously with ''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]'',<ref name="ESB storybook">''[[The Empire Strikes Back Storybook]]''</ref> prior to appearing in the film,<ref name="ESB" /> which was released [[May 21]] of the same year.<ref name="Empire Turns 40">{{ThisWeek|6UccH037VQ0|The Empire Strikes Back Turns 40, Queen's Peril Gets a Voice, and More!|sw_url=video/the-empire-strikes-back-turns-40-queen-s-peril-gets-a-voice-and-more}}</ref> The fighter was first named in [[Decipher]]'s [[1997]] ''[[Cloud City Limited]]'' expansion set of the [[Star Wars Customizable Card Game|''Star Wars'' Customizable Card Game]], though the image used to represent Obsidian 8 was not taken from the ''Empire Strikes Back'' film.<ref name="CCG" /> It was later mentioned in [[1998]]'s ''[[Star Wars: Behind the Magic]]'', where it was further identified as one of the TIE fighters from ''The Empire Strikes Back''.<ref name="BtM" />

The [[2003]] [[The Empire Strikes Back (TCG)|''The Empire Strikes Back'']] expansion set of the ''[[Star Wars Trading Card Game]]'' placed an image of the same fighter on a card which identified the fighter instead as "OS-72-8."<ref name="TCG">{{TCG|set=The Empire Strikes Back|cardname=TIE Fighter OS-72-8|link=https://swtcg.com/Content/Images/Cards/ESB/TIE_Fighter_OS_72_8.webp?v=2}}</ref> ''[[The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia]]'' from [[2008]] resolved the issue by specifying that OS-72-8 was Obsidian 8's pilot.<ref name="CSWE OS-72-8">{{CSWECite|II|426|OS-72-8}}</ref>
